post.summary: Local mode: open an owner session (HttpOnly cookie) for the web UI or the CLI
post.description: Local mode only (`ANALYZR_AUTH=local`). Sets the `analyzr_session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict); requests carrying it act as the single owner on an interactive client. The server accepts it only from localhost (Host and Origin checks). On a read-only demo (`ANALYZR_DEMO=readonly`, `Health.demo`) the session is a viewer with scope `analyzr:read` instead, accepted from the demo's public origins. A body over 4096 bytes answers 413 `payload-too-large` before it is read.

put.summary: Upload raw BPMN: 201 new model, 200 new revision or unchanged
put.description: The optional header `Analyzr-Manifest` declares the file's provenance (M6 §3.2, §3.3): the base64url of the UTF-8 JSON of an `analyzr-import/1` manifest that lists exactly this file (its `key`, if given, equal to `{key}`). The declared fields are stored on the uploaded revision; a checksum mismatch or a known tool id are `importWarnings`, the file is stored all the same. Identical bytes stay `unchanged` and keep the first revision's provenance (`provenance-kept` when the manifest declares another place in the source tool). `dryRun=true` (M6 §3.5) answers the would-be outcome with its warnings and the `impact` and writes nothing (permission `read`).

post.summary: Import up to 50 BPMN files; the model key is the pinned or the slugified path
post.description: An optional part `manifest` holds the JSON of an `analyzr-import/1` manifest (M6 §3.2; the CLI sends each batch's subset): a listed file gets the key it pins (else its path decides) and the declared provenance on its uploaded revision. A checksum mismatch, a tool id another live key already has (`external-id-moved`) and a tool id that differs from the one on the key's head (`external-id-changed`) are `importWarnings`, and so is an unchanged file whose manifest entry declares another place in the source tool than analyzr keeps (`provenance-kept`); the file is imported all the same. An invalid manifest refuses the request (422 `validation-failed`, reason `invalid-manifest`). `dryRun=true` (M6 §3.5) answers the same outcomes and the `impact` and writes nothing: permission `read`, no project lock, so a read-only token can preview a bundle. One dry run covers one request; a call into a later batch shows as unresolved.

200.description: Outcome per file (with `impact` on a dry run)

get.summary: The source-system identity of every live model (to rebuild a key map)
get.description: M6 §3.4: per live model whose head declares a source system, its key, the system, the tool id (`null` when the manifest named none) and the tool folder, as the uploaded revision declared them (an amended head is followed to its uploaded revision), sorted by key; `system` keeps one system. The integrate skill rebuilds a lost workspace's `keymap.json` from it.

parameters.description: Source system of a bundle: a lowercase slug such as `signavio` or `aris`.
parameters.name: system

get.summary: The fields of an element a model amendment can set (ETag `"r<headRev>"`)
get.description: M6 §4.8 c: per field the element allows (call target, message or signal name, start or end name, process documentation), the value on the head and on the uploaded revision, whether it can be set and why not (`only-open-questions`: no open question names it, it is neither empty nor unresolved and no live amendment set it; `expression`, `cmmn-call`, …), its live amendment, the elements reading a message name and the suggestions (processes, names with their endpoints, labels), plus the element's amendment history. An endpoint that references a message or signal yields the field of that message or signal (every endpoint referencing it changes with it); a pool resolves to its process. `ETag: "r<headRev>"` is what the save sends as `If-Match`. A deleted model, or an element the head has no fact and no amendable field for, is 404 `not-found`.

post.summary: Amend fields of a model: a new amended head (`If-Match: "r<headRev>"`; `?dryRun=true` first)
post.description: Records up to 20 amendments of one model (M6 §4.8 c) in one transaction under the project lock: the uploaded revision stays as it came, and analyzr writes an amended revision computed from its bytes by byte-preserving splices (never a bpmn-moddle round trip), checked by extracting it again; it becomes the head, with `source.kind: amendment`, its `upstream` and the plan of every live amendment. A new amendment of an element and op supersedes the live one. Events: `model.amended` (ids, elements and ops, no values), then the amended revision's `model.revised`. The new head sets off what any change from the tool does (rules, endpoint states, the relations task, the placement input); a manual link from the call to the target it now calls, and one to a `partner` whose key-tier proposal the amendment accepts, is retired by a human rejection. Each item is `recorded`, `unchanged` (identical to its live amendment) or `not-applicable` with the reason; a request with a `not-applicable` item writes nothing (422 `validation-failed`, `reason: 'amendment-not-applicable'`, the items in `items`). The answer carries the effect at the element and the cost (pairs to re-judge, a claimed relations task); `dryRun=true` computes the same and writes nothing. `If-Match: "r<headRev>"` is required (428 `precondition-required`) and checked under the lock (412 `revision-conflict` with `headRev`). Humans only and both permissions `review` and `write`: agent tokens get 403 `human-decision-required` with `reviewUrl`, a scope without both 403 `insufficient-scope`. A deleted model is 404 `not-found`.

post.summary: Withdraw every live amendment of a model in one step (humans only)
post.description: „Alle Ergänzungen dieses Modells zurücknehmen“ (M6 §4.8 c): one withdrawal row per live amendment (reason `withdrawn`, a `model.amendment_withdrawn` event each) and one re-derivation from the uploaded revision, a new revision whose bytes equal the uploaded revision's. A deleted model keeps its amendments live until withdrawn; a withdrawal there records its rows only and writes no revision. Nothing live answers 200 `unchanged`. `If-Match: "r<headRev>"` (optional) names the head the human saw and is checked under the project lock (412 `revision-conflict` with `headRev`), so an amendment recorded meanwhile is not withdrawn unseen. `dryRun=true` answers what would be withdrawn and the `cost` of the new head (pairs to re-judge, a claimed relations task) and writes nothing. Permissions `review` and `write`, humans only.

200.description: A dry run, or nothing was live (`unchanged`)

get.summary: The change list for the source tool, as Markdown or CSV (`since=<seq>`)
get.description: The amendments matching the filters, grouped per model (name and key), each with the pool or process and lane, the element's German type and name, the field, before → after, who, when and the state; a call target names its process and model, marked „Ziel nicht mehr in der Landschaft“ when no head process has that id; a shared message lists every element referencing it. Every export names the seq it reflects („Stand: Ereignis …“), and `since` lists only what was recorded or ended after it. analyzr writes nothing back to the source tool (decision 7). CSV: UTF-8 with a byte order mark, `;`-separated, CRLF, every field quoted, formula-like cells escaped.

post.summary: Withdraw one amendment („Ergänzung zurücknehmen“; humans only)
post.description: Records the withdrawal (reason `withdrawn`, a `model.amendment_withdrawn` event naming the id and op) and re-derives the head from the uploaded revision with the remaining live amendments: a new revision, with none left one whose bytes equal the uploaded revision's. On a deleted model only the row is recorded, no revision. An amendment that ended before answers 200 `unchanged`. `If-Match: "r<headRev>"` (optional) names the head of the amendment's model the human saw and is checked under the project lock (412 `revision-conflict` with `headRev`). `dryRun=true` answers the `cost` of the new head (pairs to re-judge, a claimed relations task) and writes nothing. Permissions `review` and `write`, humans only.

get.summary: Open questions: the gaps that block links and placements, from every source and the gap signals
get.description: Computed on read, never stored (M6 §4.2): relation and value chain findings, holds (note, question, label), agents' questions on proposals waiting for review, current unsure placement verdicts, no-links coded `call-target` or `collaboration`, the summaries of current submissions and the pairs they left unjudged, and the gap signals over the head facts. Questions first, then the value chain findings (`process-without-step`, `step-without-process`, `unresolved-link`), then informational items (`summary-note`, `descriptive-model`), each group ordered by `unlocks` (descending), then subject, kind and id. `modelKey` matches a model or a folder (`finanzen` matches `finanzen/mahnwesen`); `askWho` matches a lane, one of the step owners or the folder exactly. Each item carries its `actions` (M6 §4.8 a: at most one primary, German labels from code) and its `answers` (notes and outside marks); it is `answered` while a live outside mark names its id (M6 S5c-1), and `state` filters by it. An item whose call, coded end or pool flows a human, an owner's rule or the rule tier linked by an accepted relation to another process leaves the list (R1), and so does a duplicated process id while no call towards its copies waits for a decision (R1b); `listFindings` keeps listing their findings. Since UX2a each item carries its `group` (`ask` „Zu klären“, `agent` „Fragen der Agenten“, `proposal` decided on the value chain, `info` „Zur Information“; a label and a filter, never a sort key) and its question first (`text`) with the reason apart (`detail`); `group` filters (repeat it for several), `totals` counts the items per group under every filter but `group`, and `askByModel` the distinct subjects of the `ask` items per model that are neither a relation nor a placement. One question per process: a process with a held placement, an agent's question on one of its placements or an unsure verdict has no `process-without-step` item.

parameters.description: Immutable model key: lowercase slug segments separated by `/`.
parameters.name: modelKey

get.summary: The open questions as a Markdown or CSV download, with the filters of the list
get.description: Every open question matching the filters, in list order, as an attachment. Without `group`, only the `ask` items („Zu klären“, UX2a: the customer is asked what needs clarifying, not the agents' questions on proposals), unless `kind` or `source` names what to export (then every group); the file name stays `offene-fragen-<project key>` for that default. `markdown` (default): for the customer, in plain German: the date of the project's latest event („Stand 17.10.2026“) with the count of open and settled items, grouped by the contact hint (step owners, else lanes, else „Ohne Ansprechpartner“; never the folder), per item its question and reason (an agent's verbatim reason after „Laut Agent:“), „Betrifft“ with the element and the model by name, the contact hint (lanes and step owners), notes (a hold's as „Antwort“) and outside marks with their dates; the id only as an HTML comment after the heading (`<!-- q-… -->`, invisible when rendered, the way back to `analyzr questions answer`); no refs, seqs, sources or handles. `csv`: the questions without the informational items (`summary-note`, `descriptive-model`, which ask nothing), UTF-8 with a byte order mark, `;`-separated (what German spreadsheet programs open directly), CRLF, every field quoted, the columns `id`, `Art`, `Frage`, `Ansprechpartner`, `Antwort`; `Frage` holds the question, its reason as the second sentence and „Betrifft: …“; `Antwort` is empty for the customer to fill in, or holds the item's latest note (M6 S5c-1; read back, it is `unchanged`); a sheet exported before UX2a names the contact column `Ansprechpartner-Hinweis` and reads all the same. A cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab, a carriage return or their full-width forms (also after a run of `'`) gets a leading `'`, so spreadsheets never run it as a formula. The file name carries the filters (`offene-fragen-<project key>-<filters>.csv`; `state=open` adds nothing, the name says „offene“ already).

post.summary: Add a note to an open question (humans only)
post.description: Records the note („Notiz hinzufügen“, M6 §4.8 b) in the append-only `open_question_answer`; a note informs and leaves the item `open` (only an outside mark makes it `answered`, `actOnOpenQuestion`). The body is `{text}` only: S5a's `kind` is gone and gets 422. Where the text lands: on a relation (held, or proposed with an agent's question) a human note through the note use case, so the next claim of either model shows it (a hold stays until a human decides it); on a placement a human note through the placement note use case (on an agent's question the process becomes due, nothing is queued; a held placement keeps homing its process, so it is not due until a human decides the hold); anything else stays with the answer (shown and exported, it reaches no agent before M6 S7). A note identical to the id's latest note answers 200 `unchanged` and writes nothing. The text is compared and stored with LF line breaks and in Unicode NFC, trimmed; it has at most 2000 characters; a deterministic check for e-mail addresses, phone numbers and IBANs returns `warnings` and never blocks. Owner or editor on an interactive client: agent tokens get 403 `human-decision-required` with `reviewUrl`. An id that names no current open question (its source changed, which changes the id) is 404 `not-found`.

parameters.description: Id of an open question: `q-` + 16 hex characters.
parameters.name: question

200.description: An identical note was recorded earlier

post.summary: Record the answers of a filled-in sheet (`?dryRun=true` first; humans only)
post.description: The rows of the CSV the export wrote (`id`, `Antwort`; `readAnswerSheet` in `@analyzr/contracts/open-question-csv` reads them), each filled `Antwort` recorded as a note as by `answerOpenQuestion`, all in one transaction. A sheet exported before M6 S5c-1 still reads: its `Antwortart` „Liegt außerhalb der Landschaft“ (`outside-landscape`) records an outside mark with the text as its note, except on a relation or placement item (a note); „Antwort“, „Wird im Modell ergänzt“ and an empty cell record a note. Rows with an empty answer are ignored (counted only); an id that names no current open question (also one whose source changed since the export) is listed `unknown` and never stored; a row with a text over 2000 characters, control characters, an unknown `Antwortart` or an id an earlier row answers is listed `invalid` and never stored; a note identical to the item's latest note, or a mark on an item a live mark marks, is `unchanged`. `row` is the position in `rows`. `dryRun=true` lists the same and stores nothing. At most 5000 rows and 4194304 bytes per call (413 `payload-too-large` above).

200.description: What the sheet stored or would store

post.summary: Act on an open question: link, place, choose the valid copy, mark outside (humans)
post.description: Runs one of the item's `actions` (M6 §4.8 a) in one transaction under the project lock, through the use cases that exist. `link`: per target a live typed relation between the anchor and the target (proposed or held: a rule-tier or key-tier proposal, an agent's) is accepted as the human's decision, else an accepted `manual` relation is written (a pool's flows: one per anchor, directed like its flow); the rationale is German and from code („Aus „Offene Fragen“: …“) plus the note. `place`: a manual placement, accepted at once. `choose-copy`: the calls towards the copies are accepted towards the valid copy and rejected towards the others, all or nothing with their versions (409 `conflict` otherwise); with `placeOthersOutside` the other copies without a home step go to `@outside`; the note is a note on the item. `outside`: an outside mark (an `open_question_answer` of kind `outside-landscape`, its text the note or null); while a live mark exists, 200 `unchanged`. The answer names the relations and placements written (`manual`: „Rückgängig“ rejects them through the decision routes) or decided, and the item as the list now shows it (`null` when the action took it off). An id that names no current item is 404 `not-found`; an action the item does not offer is 422 `validation-failed` with `reason: 'action-not-offered'`. Owner or editor on an interactive client: agent tokens get 403 `human-decision-required` with `reviewUrl`.

post.summary: Withdraw an outside mark („Rückgängig“; humans only)
post.description: Ends an outside mark of the item (M6 §4.8 b) with a row in the append-only `open_question_answer_withdrawal` and an `open_question.answer_withdrawn` event; the mark no longer counts, so the item is `open` again unless another live mark names it, and marking again records a new mark. A mark withdrawn before answers 200 `unchanged`. Only outside marks are withdrawn (a note is 422 `validation-failed` with `reason: 'not-an-outside-mark'`); an id that names no current item, or an answer of another item, is 404 `not-found`. Owner or editor on an interactive client: agent tokens get 403 `human-decision-required` with `reviewUrl`.

put.description: Saves the document as the next revision (humans only). `If-Match: "r<rev>"` must name the head revision: without it 428 `precondition-required`, a stale one 412 `revision-conflict` with `headRev`; content equal to the head answers 200 `unchanged` whatever the `If-Match`. `If-None-Match: *` creates (or revives) the chain instead: 201, or 412 `revision-conflict` if it exists. `dryRun=true` checks the same and returns the impact (removed and changed steps with their placements) without writing anything. The body is the `.vc.json` document as `application/json`, at most 2 MiB; its canonical form may have at most 1 MiB (`document-too-large`).

post.summary: Claim up to 5 queued analysis tasks (15-minute lease, analyzr:propose)
post.description: Claims queued tasks (and tasks whose lease expired with attempts left), oldest first, in the projects where the caller may propose (`projectId` narrows it), of the kinds the caller handles (`kinds`, default `["relations"]`), with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. Each item carries its `kind`, a lease token (shown once, bound to the task and the caller) and the compact claim input, rendered in the claim transaction. A `relations` item: the current agent judgements on pairs touching the model (`judged`) and the pairs a partner analysis judges (`skip`), both left out of `candidates`; the remaining `rule`, `key` and `lexical` candidates and the relations in neither list, accepted pairs, unchanged rejections and missing ends aside, are the task’s assignment, and the other `compatible` candidates the search space for missing partners. A `placement` item (`analyzr-claim-placement/1`): the chain’s steps, the open processes whose input changed since an agent last judged them (at most 50, `truncated` when more are due) with their proposals and the human decisions, and accepted placements as examples. Empty when nothing is claimable.

get.summary: Claimable tasks per project; `wait=1..30` long-polls until work arrives

post.summary: Submit the result of a claimed task (idempotent by submissionId)
post.description: A `relations` task: validates every item (refs in the head facts, one endpoint in the task model, endpoint kinds, limits) and answers per relation `applied`, `duplicate`, `suppressed`, `reopened` or `invalid:<reason>`, per no-link `stored`, `duplicate` or `invalid:<reason>`, and the assigned pairs left unjudged (`uncovered`). Earlier pipeline proposals and no-links on pairs touching the model that were judged on another version of the model or under another procedure are withdrawn; current judgements stay. A `placement` task (`kind: "placement"` in the result): per placement and unsure item an outcome, the withdrawn stale or replaced pipeline proposals, the input processes left without a verdict (`skipped`) and whether a follow-up task was queued. 422 `wrong-task-kind` (items of the other kind); 409 `lease-lost` (another holder, a release, a wrong token), `task-cancelled` (new revision), `already-submitted` (another submissionId).

post.summary: Create an auto-accept rule (owner, interactive client; off unless `enabled`)
post.description: Revision 1 of a new rule, authored by the caller: while it is enabled, agent proposals recorded afterwards that meet it are accepted as decisions of the author (never retroactive: open proposals need `apply`). 422 `validation-failed` with `reason` `unknown-agent` or `name-taken`; a draft the schema refuses (a tier of another kind, a type on a placement rule, a confidence outside 0.5–1, control characters) is 422 `validation-failed` with `errors` naming the fields instead.

post.summary: What a rule (saved or not) would have accepted so far and would accept now
post.description: Replays the project history: the agent proposals humans decided that the rule would have accepted, with the humans’ verdicts (an empirical precision; acceptances by auto-accept rules are no ground truth and counted apart), the open proposals it would accept now (what `apply` would do) with the blocked ones per reason, and a curve over minimum confidences. Nothing is written.

get.summary: One auto-accept rule with every revision (ETag `"r<revision>"`)

put.summary: Edit, enable or disable a rule: a new revision (`If-Match: "r<revision>"` required)
put.description: Writes the draft as the next immutable revision, authored by the caller (decisions already recorded keep their revision). `If-Match` must name the head revision: without it 428 `precondition-required`, a stale one 412 `revision-conflict` with `headRev`. A draft equal to the head answers `unchanged`, unless the head’s author is no longer an owner: then the caller takes the rule over (a new revision with the same fields). The kind of a rule never changes (422 `validation-failed` with `reason` `kind-changed`); otherwise the reasons and `errors` of the create route.

post.summary: Apply an enabled rule to the open proposals (`?dryRun=true` first)
post.description: Evaluates the head revision against every open proposal of its kind, with every safeguard. `dryRun=true` lists what it would accept and what is blocked. The real call needs the head `revision`, an enabled rule whose author is still an owner, and `expectedCount` equal to the fresh count: 409 `conflict` with `count`, `revision` and `reason` (`rule-disabled`, `author-not-owner`, `revision-changed`, `count-changed`) otherwise; 422 `validation-failed` with `reason` `expected-count-required` without `revision` and `expectedCount`. The result says whether the head is enabled and its author still an owner.

200.description: What it did or would do

post.summary: Revoke auto-acceptances by rule, agent, kind or ids (`?dryRun=true` first)
post.description: Each acceptance still in force is withdrawn (a human withdrawal under the decision’s principal): its item returns to `proposed` while a live proposal remains, else it turns `obsolete` and the agents judge it again. Items a human decided since are never touched. The real call needs `expectedCount` equal to the fresh count (409 `conflict`; 422 `validation-failed` with `reason` `expected-count-required` without it).

200.description: What it did or would do

Readable by editors and owners on an interactive client (permission `review`), so every reviewer sees which acceptances were made by a rule; agent tokens get 403 `human-decision-required`. The rules themselves stay owner-only.
